subject: physiology
title: Autonomic nervous system

steps.tx: The **autonomic nervous system** divides into sympathetic outflow from T1 to L2 through chains, parasympathetic outflow from cranial nerves III, VII, IX and X and sacral segments, and the semi independent enteric gut brain. Preganglionic fibres release acetylcholine onto nicotinic receptors, postganglionic sympathetic fibres release noradrenaline onto alpha and beta receptors, and the adrenal medulla spills adrenaline into blood. Resting tone is parasympathetic for rest and digest, and diabetes or amyloid can cripple the whole system.
steps.say: Think of two opposing outflows plus a gut brain that runs itself: sympathetic fibres leave the thoracolumbar cord and relay noradrenaline, parasympathetic fibres leave by cranial nerves and sacral cord and relay acetylcholine. The comparison image sets fibre lengths and transmitters side by side, with the adrenal medulla pouring adrenaline straight into blood. At rest the parasympathetic side dominates digestion and heart rate, and diseases such as diabetes can blunt both sides.

vis.alt: Two column comparison of sympathetic and parasympathetic outflow: sympathetic from T1 to L2 with short preganglionic fibres and long noradrenergic postganglionic fibres, parasympathetic from cranial nerves III VII IX X and S2 to S4 with long preganglionic fibres and short cholinergic postganglionic fibres.
vis.caption: Sympathetic: thoracolumbar, short pre, long post, noradrenaline. Parasympathetic: craniosacral, long pre, short post, acetylcholine.

steps.tx: **Muscarinic receptors** of M3 type contract gut and eye and drive glands, nicotinic receptors serve ganglia and muscle as Nn and Nm, alpha one receptors constrict vessels and dilate the pupil, beta one receptors race and strengthen the heart, and beta two receptors relax bronchi and uterus. Atropine dries and blinds with tachycardia, beta blockers lower rate and mask hypoglycaemia, and tamsulosin relaxes the prostate but flops the iris. Nitric oxide fills erectile tissue, vasoactive intestinal peptide secretes in gut, and neuropeptide Y tightens vessels.
steps.say: Receptors decide what each transmitter achieves: M3 squeezes gut and glands, alpha one squeezes vessels, beta one drives the heart, and beta two opens airways, a pattern the receptor table maps to G proteins. Atropine blocks muscarinic effects leaving a dry mouth, wide pupils and fast pulse, beta blockers slow the heart but hide low sugar warnings, and tamsulosin relaxes the prostate. Other messengers complete the list, including nitric oxide, vasoactive peptide and neuropeptide Y.

vis.alt: Table of autonomic receptors with G protein pathway and effects: alpha-1 Gq vasoconstriction, alpha-2 Gi, beta-1 Gs raising heart rate, beta-2 Gs relaxing bronchi, M2 Gi slowing the heart, M3 Gq contracting gut and glands, nicotinic ganglionic and muscle channels.
vis.caption: Gq: alpha-1 and M3 (constrict, secrete). Gs: beta-1 and beta-2 (heart, relax). Gi: M2 and alpha-2.

steps.tx: The **baroreflex** senses stretch in the carotid sinus: high pressure fires vagal slowing, straining in Valsalva shows phases with overshoot, and standing normally drops systolic by twenty and diastolic by ten before correction. Carotid massage can break supraventricular tachycardia, Horner syndrome gives ptosis, miosis and anhidrosis, Adie pupil reacts tonically to near, Argyll Robertson pupil accommodates but not to light in neurosyphilis, and postural tachycardia syndrome races in the young needing fluids and salt. The bladder detrusor squeezes by muscarinic drive while the sphincter holds by alpha drive.
steps.say: Stretch receptors in the carotid sinus complete the loop in the diagram: pressure rises, vagal traffic brakes the heart, and vessels relax, while standing reverses the signal. Bedside patterns include Horner syndrome with a small pupil and drooping lid, tonic Adie pupils, and the light near dissociation of neurosyphilis. Valsalva phases, carotid massage for fast rhythms, and bladder control by opposing detrusor and sphincter receptors all test the same reflex machinery.

vis.alt: Baroreceptor reflex loop: raised blood pressure stretches carotid sinus and aortic arch receptors, afferents via IX and X reach the nucleus tractus solitarius, which increases vagal tone and reduces sympathetic outflow, lowering heart rate and vessel tone and so pressure.
vis.caption: Rising pressure fires baroreceptors, which brake the heart through the vagus and relax vessels; standing does the opposite.

steps.tx: **Autonomic failure** in pure failure pairs alpha synuclein with supine hypertension, multiple system atrophy adds stridor and acted out dreams, and diabetes adds gastroparesis, cystopathy and impotence. Dysreflexia above T6 pounds with headache needing the patient seated, nifedipine bitten and swallowed, while midodrine presses on standing, fludrocortisone retains salt, and pyridostigmine boosts ganglia. Tilt tables provoke, sweat testing maps, Valsalva ratios split causes, and loss of night dipping on twenty four hour readings confirms failure in elderly patients on many drugs.
steps.say: When autonomic control fails, standing pressure collapses while lying pressure may soar, a combination seen in pure autonomic failure and multiple system atrophy with its stridor and dream enactment. The dysreflexia panel shows the emergency above a T6 cord injury: a full bladder triggers a hypertensive surge that needs sitting up, trigger removal and rapid pressure control. Tilt testing, sweat mapping and drug review with midodrine or fludrocortisone guide longer care.

vis.alt: Autonomic dysreflexia in spinal injury above T6: a stimulus below the lesion, usually a full bladder or bowel, causes a sympathetic surge with severe hypertension; baroreflex slows the heart but cannot relax vessels below the lesion; treat by sitting up, removing the stimulus and lowering the pressure.
vis.caption: Spinal cord injury at or above T6: noxious stimulus below the lesion leads to severe hypertension; sit up and remove the trigger.
